newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sexy Austrian lingerie to make Gulf Arab debut.
newsitem.headline: Sexy Austrian lingerie to make Gulf Arab debut.

text.p: Austrian luxury lingerie chain Palmers will slink into the Gulf this week when its sexy selections make their debut in the United Arab Emirates, the owner of the UAE franchise said on Sunday.
The region's first Palmers outlet is due to open in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the oil-rich UAE, on Wednesday to coincide with the final days of the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan.

But the eye-catching posters of scantily-clad supermodels which are the company's trademark in Austria will not be seen in the traditional UAE, where many women are dressed in long black robes and veiled in public.

"We'll have advertising, but appropriate for the local standard. The models would, for example, be wearing nightgowns instead of underwear," said Rashid Mohammad al-Mazroui, chairman of the Al-Mazroui Group which holds the local franchise.
Mazroui said he had consciously decided to open the family-owned Austrian chain during Ramadan.
"Ramadan is a good month in a religious sense and people buy more in Ramadan, especially local people," he said.
A branch in the UAE's commercial centre Dubai is due to open in March, followed by one in the eastern oasis city of Al-Ain at the end of the year. A second Dubai shop will open in 1998.
Mazroui said stores would mainly cater to a local clientele, but hoped foreigners -- who make up more than 75 percent of the UAE's 2.4 million inhabitants -- would shop there too.
Mazroui was optimistic the stores would be a success.

"Palmers will be cheaper than other lingerie stores in the UAE," he said. "We will have a very big range, including ladies' lingerie, children's underwear, swimming costumes and men's underwear at a separate outlet."
Mazroui said the shops would be exact replicas of the stores in Austria, where buxom mannequins with pouting lips display Palmers array of lace and lycra.
Palmers Austria had turnover of $280 million in 1995, with 13 percent earned in outlets abroad.
